content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.
When this app is finished, what should be different from how you handle bookmarks today? What problem are you hoping it solves?

Honestly, right now my bookmarks are a mess. I save links in my browser and then I never find them again — they're just a giant unsorted pile, and half the time I've forgotten what a link even was because it's just a title I don't remember.

So what I really want is a place where I can save a link and it actually helps me. When I paste in a web address, I'd love for it to go grab the details on its own — the page's title, a little description, maybe the site's icon or a picture — so I'm not stuck staring at a bare URL later trying to remember what it was.

Then I want to actually be able to organize and find things. Being able to put labels on links so I can group them, and a real search that digs through everything I've saved, matters a lot to me. And a "read this later" pile that I can look at on its own, separate from everything else, would be great.

That's the heart of it: save a link easily, have it remember what the link actually is, and be able to find it again later without the mess I have now.

content: If the original page later changes its title, description, icon, or picture, should your saved bookmark keep the details you reviewed—including your edits—rather than silently replacing them?

Yes — once I've saved a bookmark, the details are mine. Whatever I reviewed and especially anything I changed myself should stay put, even if the original page later renames itself or swaps its picture. The whole reason I fix up a title is to make it recognizable *to me*; it would be maddening if I came back later and my careful wording had been quietly overwritten by whatever the site decided to call itself this month.

So my answer is a clear yes: don't silently replace what I've got. My saved copy should hold onto the title, description, icon, and picture as I left them.

The one nuance I'd add: if a page really has changed and I happen to *want* the fresh details, I'd like that to be something I choose — like a "refresh from the page" I can reach for on purpose — not something that just happens to me behind my back. But the default, and the thing that matters most, is that my reviewed and edited details are kept and never overwritten on their own.

content: If an original page later disappears or is temporarily unavailable, should opening it simply leave your bookmark intact—so you can keep its saved details, notes, and labels and try the page again later?

Yes, absolutely. A page being down — whether it's just having a bad day or gone for good — should never cost me my bookmark. Everything I put into it is mine: the title and description I reviewed, my notes, my labels. Losing all that just because the far end is unreachable would be the worst thing the app could do, since a link that's gone flaky is often exactly the one where my saved details and notes have become the only record I've got. So opening a dead or unreachable page should just fail to open the page, quietly, and leave my bookmark completely untouched so I can try again another day.

While you raise it, here's a related wish that this situation brings to mind for me: when a page truly vanishes, the saved title and my notes help, but sometimes what I really wanted was the *content* of the page itself. So it would be reassuring if, at the time I save a link, the app could quietly keep its own copy of the page — so that if the original ever disappears, I can still read what I saved, not just my notes about it. I don't need to design that now, but keeping the bookmark intact is the floor, and having a kept copy to fall back on would be the thing that truly saves me.
